questions.question: Read the Passage carefully & answer the following questions: Raksha Bandhan is a traditional Hindu festival that celebrates the unique bond of protection and affection between brothers and sisters. The name "Raksha Bandhan" literally means "the knot of protection" and is marked by a sacred ritual in which a sister ties a decorative thread, known as a rakhi, around her brother’s wrist. This act represents the sister’s prayers for her brother’s well-being and the brother’s promise to protect her. The festival is observed on the full moon day of the Hindu month of Shravana, usually in August. The origins of Raksha Bandhan are rooted in mythology and legendary tales. In the Mahabharata, Lord Krishna once injured his finger during a battle, and Draupadi, wife of the Pandavas, immediately tore off a piece of her sari to bandage it. Deeply moved by her gesture, Krishna vowed to protect her in every circumstance. Another story recounts how Goddess Lakshmi tied a rakhi to the demon king Bali to safeguard her husband Vishnu. Historically, the rakhi symbolized ties of protection beyond blood relations, linking friends, rulers, and well-wishers. Today, Raksha Bandhan is celebrated both physically and virtually, with siblings exchanging gifts and sweets. The festival transcends religious and cultural boundaries in India, reinforcing bonds of duty, care, and affection. Across the globe, Indian communities continue to uphold this tradition as an emblem of love and protection. Q1. Convert the passive sentence from the passage — "A rakhi is tied by a sister around her brother’s wrist" — into active voice.
